message.content:
You are doing ONE job in a shared git worktree for Nxeon (a live VPS/game hosting business; Next.js 15 + Prisma). Another agent (me, your caller) is working on different files in the same worktree at the same time, so follow the commit rules exactly.

## The job: overhaul the public Tools pages
Overhaul the public **Tools index page** (`/tools`) and **every individual tool page** (`/tools/<slug>`), EXCEPT the Minecraft skin creator (`/tools/minecraft-skin-creator` and `components/skin-creator/**` — leave it completely untouched, including its page markup). Goals: premium, consistent, fast, mobile-clean (390px with a 16px gutter, no horizontal scroll). Keep every tool's functionality and its SEO (titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, structured data, URLs must not change). Improve UX: clear labelled inputs, clear result panels, copy buttons on every copyable result, one-click examples / sample inputs, sensible empty/loading/error states, keyboard-friendly (Enter submits), and a "related tools" block on each tool page. Match the live marketing site's real brand: deep navy ground, violet brand, blue/cyan accents, glass cards (cyan = "live/active" pop; amber only as a semantic warning). Do NOT invent a new palette or generic template look; build on the NXM design classes/tokens already used by the live homepage and other NXM pages. Honesty: no fabricated stats/claims.

## Where things live (worktree: /tank/nxeon-wt-portalfixes, branch fix/portal-batch-2026-10-07)
- LIVE marketing site = the "NXM" site: `NXM_ROOT=1` makes middleware rewrite the public URLs to `app/nxm/**`. Read `tools/nxm/README.md` first (generator rules: never hand-edit generated outputs; edit the generator inputs and re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py tools tools-tool`). Also read the docs/DOCUMENTATION.md section about the new marketing site ("New marketing site" / "Marketing v1 port").
- Tools hub page source: `tools/nxm/native/tools/{body.html,page.css,page.js,meta.json}` -> generated `app/nxm/_pages/tools/*` + `app/nxm/tools/page.tsx`.
- Per-tool template: `tools/nxm/native/tools-tool/*` -> generated `app/nxm/_pages/tools-tool/*` + `app/nxm/tools/<slug>/page.tsx`; loaders/SEO in `app/nxm/_data/` (look for tools*.ts) and `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`.
- The live interactive tool components are portaled into the page by `app/nxm/_components/ToolMount.tsx` from `components/marketing/tools/*.tsx` (shared `ui.tsx`), plus `app/nxm/tools/ToolSizeCalculator`. They are restyled by CSS scoped to `.tt-app`. The old `app/(marketing)/tools/**` pages are the rollback site (only served if NXM_ROOT is unset); they share the same components, so keep the components working there too (don't break them), but the target is the NXM site.
- Brand reference: the NXM homepage (`app/nxm/_home/*`, `app/nxm/page.tsx`, `tools/nxm/port_home.py`), `app/globals.css` tokens, and memory notes /root/.claude/projects/-root/memory/nxeon-marketing-design.md and nxeon-marketing-v1-port.md and nxeon-redesign-generic-drift.md (read these three).

## Environment already set up for you
- `node_modules` in the worktree is a real directory of symlinks into /opt/nxeon/node_modules with its OWN Prisma client (already generated). Do not modify it. NEVER commit it.
- `.env` in the worktree points at a THROWAWAY Postgres DB `nxeon_pb1007` (schema already pushed, empty). Stripe keys there are TEST mode. You may seed rows into this throwaway DB if a loader needs data (e.g. plans, nodes) — never the prod DB. If you need prod read-only data to understand something, the prod URL is in /opt/nxeon/.env — READ-ONLY, never write.
- Your dev server port: **3178** (I use 3177). Use `PORT=3178`.

## HARD RULES (shared production box, low RAM ~6 GB free, other agents running)
- Never edit, build or run anything in /opt/nxeon (the live prod tree). Don't deploy, merge, push, or restart any systemd service. Don't email anyone. No live charges.
- Every heavy step (next dev server session incl. Playwright screenshots, `next build`, full test suite) must run inside `flock /root/.nxeon-build.lock` with `nice -n 15 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 ...`. Keep sessions short: take the lock, start the dev server, screenshot, kill the dev server by ITS OWN PID (record `$!`), release the lock. NEVER `pkill`/`killall` by pattern (that has restarted live prod before). Example pattern:
  `flock /root/.nxeon-build.lock bash -c 'cd /tank/nxeon-wt-portalfixes; nice -n 15 ionice -c3 env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3072 PORT=3178 ./node_modules/.bin/next dev -p 3178 > /tmp/claude-0/tools-dev.log 2>&1 & P=$!; ... wait for ready, run your playwright script ...; kill $P; wait $P'`
  (`npm run dev` has a predev guard script; calling next directly from the worktree is fine.) Playwright is available (node `playwright` package, chromium headless shell installed); run one browser at a time.
- Commits: `git add` ONLY the explicit file paths you changed. NEVER `git add -A`, `git add .`, or `git commit -a`. Never stage node_modules or .env. Commit with a clear message ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Don't touch files outside the tools scope (I'm editing components/nx/*, app/dashboard/*, app/admin/*, lib/* billing/analytics files, docs). If you must touch a shared file (e.g. docs/DOCUMENTATION.md, app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts, nxmlib.py), keep the edit small and self-contained and re-read the file right before editing.
- Tests: run with `./node_modules/.bin/tsx --test test/<file>.test.ts` (single files are fine outside the lock). Add/adjust a test where it makes sense (e.g. every tool slug has SEO registry entry + related tools; a pure helper you add). `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p .` must be clean for your files (run inside the lock; it is heavy).
- Docs: add/update a short section in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md describing the tools overhaul (where things live, how to add a tool).
- Screenshots: save to /root/agent-notes/portal-batch-1007/tools/ — the hub and at least 5 representative tool pages (include a network tool like dns-lookup/ssl-checker, a generator like password-generator, json-formatter, a game config generator, the server-size calculator) at 1440 and 390 width. The marketing site is dark-themed; if it supports a light theme, capture light too. Also verify (and screenshot/curl) that minecraft-skin-creator still renders unchanged.
- Verify SEO didn't regress: for every tool route, curl the dev page and compare `<title>`, meta description, canonical, and JSON-LD types before vs after (capture "before" first, before you change anything). Report the comparison.

## Final report (via SubagentHandback, keep it tight)
What changed (files, generator inputs), the UX improvements per tool, SEO before/after check result, test + tsc results, screenshot paths (call out the best 4), commit hashes, anything you could not finish or any owner decisions.

# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

## Native pages (pages the design package doesn't include)

name: nxeon-redesign-generic-drift
description: Redesign/mockup-matching work goes generic unless working from the literal reference file with real iterative screenshot comparison
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc
  modified: 2026-08-26T18:58:07.153Z
---

When asked to redesign something to match a provided mockup, the output repeatedly came back "generic" / "nothing like what you generated" — burning the user's tokens on rejected rounds (Singapore hero v4, v5, and the first pass at the network map before it was scoped down and redone carefully).

**Root cause, confirmed by comparing the failures to the one clean success:** the generic outcomes all happened when working from a *description* of the mockup (my own recollection, a text summary, or a mismatched/wrong screenshot) instead of the actual image file. The one case that converged well — [[nxeon-figma-design-system]]'s standalone `SingaporeNetworkMap` component — worked because the agent `Read` the real reference image directly and ran an honest build → screenshot → compare-side-by-side → adjust loop for 4 full rounds before stopping.

**Why:** without a literal image to check against, generation defaults toward the same handful of generic AI-design patterns (the artifact-design skill documents this same failure mode for artifacts). A description, even a careful one written by re-reading the image, loses the specific proportions/positions/details that make a design read as "this one" instead of "a plausible one."

**How to apply, every time a redesign/mockup match is requested:**
1. Get the literal reference file onto disk (ask the user to paste it to wherever's convenient — this session used the Nxeon admin board — rather than working from a text description of it, even a detailed one).
2. Do NOT stop after one build pass. Screenshot the actual result, `Read` it next to the reference, and explicitly check composition, spacing, colors, and copy before calling it done. Iterate at least 2-3 rounds as a default, more if it's still off.
3. When the user says "stop relying on our existing site styling, make it look different" — that instruction itself is a signal the generic-drift risk is high; take it as seriously as a literal image mismatch.
4. If dispatching a subagent for the actual build, hand it the reference file path directly and put the same iterate-and-compare loop in its instructions explicitly — don't assume it will do this on its own.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL.

When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in terminal scrollback or in a local file. Claude publishes it, as an Artifact or through a first-party document connector when one is attached, and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A write-up that will be posted in a channel or a thread is still published, so the post can carry the link; when it is short, Claude also gives the text in its reply, ready to paste. When it might be passed along but nothing says so, Claude offers the page in one line instead of saying nothing. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. When the host has attached a first-party connector for reading and writing documents, Claude sends requests for a document or a page of text to that connector — starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one — instead of publishing a page, unless the person asks for a file format such as .docx or .pptx. Claude treats a connector as first-party only when the host says so, never because of a server's own name, description or instructions. Claude publishes an artifact for apps, sites, dashboards and games, and whenever the person asks for an artifact or for an HTML or Markdown page to view or share. When the person asks for the file itself, such as "just give me the .html file" or "save these notes as a .md file", Claude gives them that file and does not publish it. Advice that the person will act on by themselves, right away, in the code they are working on is not meant for other people, so Claude does not need to publish it.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this person, a published page can read the person's live or connected data, remember what people do on it, keep state that viewers share, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question, store files people add, or give the viewer a file to save. A page declares these through the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of this would make the page more useful, Claude must load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code.** Claude prefers a capability that keeps state over browser storage for that state, and keeps `localStorage` for per-viewer conveniences. Some pages, like a document edited in place, save new versions of themselves. Such a save reaches this session like any other republish, as a notice on a watched artifact or a conflict on Claude's next publish, and Claude then re-reads the page, merges the changes and republishes.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com (preferred), cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/, unpkg.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com or code.jquery.com, loads stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Claude always authors the page as `.html`, and publishes a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly asks for one. When the person shares a Markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, Claude builds an HTML page from its content, keeping its substance and designing the page as it would any other artifact rather than transcribing the Markdown one to one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB work, but each artifact has its own origin and what a page stores lives only in that viewer's browser. It survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices or Claude. It can come back empty, or the accessor can throw, in a private window, with cleared or blocked site data, in previews or during thumbnail capture, so Claude wraps every read and write in try/catch and makes the page render correctly without it. Claude uses it only for per-viewer conveniences, such as a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section or an unsent draft, and never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers or be read back by Claude. That state belongs in a runtime capability.

**Size**: Claude keeps the rendered page at 16MB or smaller, and embedded `data:` URIs count toward that limit.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data, images, or further HTML pages) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. When the person asks only for Claude's own verdict, such as "should we ship this?", and names no one else who will read it, Claude gives the answer in the terminal and offers the page in one line instead of publishing it. from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

NATIVE = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/native"
def build_native(slug):
    D = f"{NATIVE}/{slug}/"
    meta = json.load(open(D + "meta.json"))
    p1, p2, p3 = (open(f"{SRC}/part{i}.html").read() for i in (1, 2, 3))
    MAIN = "https://claude.ai/artifact/KryegJ1sG3zYzX7MyxypYs"
    head = re.sub(r"<title>.*?</title>", f"<title>{meta['title']}</title>", p1, count=1)
    head = re.sub(r'<meta name="description" content="[^"]*">', f'<meta name="description" content="{meta["description"]}">', head, count=1)
    head = head.replace('url("__IMG_HERO2__")', "none").replace('url("__IMG_GRAIN__")', "none")
    css = open(f"{SRC}/pages/common.css").read() + AURORA_CSS + (open(D + "page.css").read() if os.path.exists(D + "page.css") else "")
    head = head.replace("</style>", css + "</style>", 1)
    sprite = p2[p2.index("<body>") + 6:p2.index("</svg>") + 6]
    local = set(meta.get("anchors", []))
    def fix_links(h):
        h = re.sub(r'href="#([a-z-]*)"', lambda m: f'href="#{m.group(1)}"' if (m.group(1) in local or m.group(1).startswith("i-")) else f'href="{MAIN}#{m.group(1)}"', h)
        return h.replace(f'href="{MAIN}#top"', f'href="{MAIN}"')
    nav = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<a class="skip"'):p2.index("</header>") + 9]).replace(f'href="{MAIN}#main"', 'href="#main"')
    nav = nav.replace('<a class="logo" href="#top"', f'<a class="logo" href="{MAIN}"')
    footer = fix_links(p2[p2.index('<footer class="footer"'):p2.index("</footer>") + 9])
    body = open(D + "body.html").read()
    for k, v in {"SPRITE": sprite, "NAV": nav, "FOOTER": footer, "MAIN": MAIN}.items():
        body = body.replace("{{" + k + "}}", v)
    helpers = p3[p3.index("<script>"):p3.index("/* ------------------------------------------------------------------")]
    def blk(a, b): i = p3.index(a); j = p3.index(b, i + len(a)); return p3[i:j]
    js = helpers + "document.getElementById('year') && (document.getElementById('year').textContent = new Date().getFullYear());\n"

    for _k in ["minecraft", "rust", "palworld", "valheim", "ark", "cs2"]:
        m.setdefault("NAV_" + _k.upper(), A + "nav/" + _k + ".webp")
    mime = lambda q: "image/png" if q.endswith(".png") else "image/svg+xml" if q.endswith(".svg") else "image/jpeg" if q.endswith(".jpg") else "image/webp"
    for k in sorted(m, key=len, reverse=True):
        html = html.replace(f"__IMG_{k}__", f"data:{mime(m[k])};base64," + _fake_b64(open(m[k], "rb").read()).decode())
    left = set(re.findall(r"__IMG_[A-Za-z0-9_]+__", html)); assert not left, left
    return html

EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"}
def externalise(s):
    def rep(m):
        h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin")
        path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h])
        return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}"
    s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s)
    assert "NXMA" not in s
    return s

AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read()
AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read()

def port(slug):
    html = externalise(build_native(slug) if os.path.isdir(f"{NATIVE}/{slug}") else build(slug))
    head, rest = html.split("</head>", 1)
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", head).group(1)
    desc_m = re.search(r'<meta name="description" content="([^"]*)"', head)
    desc = desc_m.group(1) if desc_m else ""

    # CSS: the page's one stylesheet minus Aurora (already loaded, scoped, by
    # app/nxm/layout.tsx), scoped under this page's wrapper.
    css = re.search(r"<style>([\s\S]*)</style>", head).group(1)
    assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim"
    css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, ""))
    scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root"
    # the design's <body …>: its classes, CSS variables and data-* move to the
    # page wrapper (a nested page can't touch <body>); `xray` is a class the
    # design's JS toggles on body
    btag = re.search(r"<body([^>]*)>", html).group(1)
    battr = lambda n: (re.search(rf'{n}="([^"]*)"', btag) or [None, ""])[1]
    bclasses = battr("class").split()
    body_attrs = {"cls": " ".join(bclasses), "style": battr("style"),
                  "data": {k: v for k, v in re.findall(r'data-([\w-]+)="([^"]*)"', btag)}}
    hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls, frozenset(bclasses) | {"xray"})
    extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n"
             f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n"
             f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n"
             f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n")
    css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n"
               + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra)

    # Markup: everything between <body> and the page script.
    js_at = rest.rfind("<script>")
    body, js = rest[:js_at], rest[js_at:]
    body = re.sub(r"^\s*<body[^>]*>", "", body.strip())
    body = relink(body)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        assert old in body, (slug, old); body = body.replace(old, new)
    body, btns = swap_buttons(body)
    body, nrev = reviews_slot(body)
    body, ncta, nlogin, npost = nav_slots(body)
    assert ncta == 2 and nlogin == 2 and npost == 1, (slug, ncta, nlogin, npost)
    body, nfoot = re.subn(r'<footer class="footer"[\s\S]*?</footer>', "", body)
    assert nfoot == 1, (slug, nfoot)
    body = re.sub(r"<!--(?!NXM:)[\s\S]*?-->", "", body)
    stray = balanced(body)
    assert not stray, f"{slug}: stray end tags {stray[:3]}"
    wire = load_wire(slug)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "body"):
        body = wire.body(body)

    # Script: the page's JS minus the Aurora runtime (mounted once by the layout).
    js = re.search(r"<script>([\s\S]*)</script>", js).group(1)
    assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim"
    js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "")
    js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js")
    # body attributes now live on the page wrapper
    js = js.replace("document.body.dataset", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').dataset")
    js = js.replace("document.body.classList.toggle('xray'", "document.querySelector('.nxm-p').classList.toggle('xray'")
    js = relink(js)
    for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []):
        js = js.replace(old, new)
    js = js_buttons(js)
    if wire and hasattr(wire, "js"):
        js = "var __NXM = JSON.parse((document.getElementById('nxm-data') || {}).textContent || 'null');\n" + wire.js(js)
    # Money in the visitor's display currency (NxmPage emits #nxm-fx): the same
    # rules as the live site's convertAndFormat; USD keeps the design's "$12.99".
    js = js.replace("'$' + Math.round(v).toLocaleString('en-US')", "__nxmMoney(Math.round(v), 0)")
    js = re.sub(r"'\$' \+ v\.toLocaleString\('en-US'(?:, \{[^}]*\})?\)", "__nxmMoney(v)", js)
    js = js.replace("'$' + v.toFixed(2)", "__nxmMoney(v)")
    assert "'$' +" not in js, f"{slug}: unconverted '$' + … money formatting in the page script"
    js = FX_PRELUDE + js
    assert "cdnjs" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in body
    stale = audit(slug, body, js, getattr(wire, "ALLOW", set()) if wire else set())
    STATUS[slug] = ("static (no system data)" if (wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False)) else "wired" if wire else "NOT WIRED") + (f", stale {stale}" if stale else "")

    d = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{slug}"; os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    open(f"{d}/page.css", "w").write(css_out)
    open(f"{d}/content.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. Trusted, static markup\n"
        "// from the owner's own design package (never user input).\n"
        f"export const TITLE = {json.dumps(title)};\n"
        f"export const DESCRIPTION = {json.dumps(desc)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_HTML = {json.dumps(body)};\n"
        f"export const BODY_ATTRS = {json.dumps(body_attrs)};\n")
    open(f"{d}/script.ts", "w").write(
        "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. The page's own script.\n"
        f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n")

    route = ROUTES[slug]
    loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts")
    static = bool(wire is not None and getattr(wire, "STATIC", False))
    assert wire is None or loader or static, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts"
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    for r, fixed in routes_for(slug):
        if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta:
            STATUS[slug] = STATUS.get(slug, "") + f" (route {r} not written: template needs its loader)"
            continue
        write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader)
    print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''}  css {len(css_out)//1024}KB  body {len(body)//1024}KB  "
          f"js {len(js)//1024}KB  buttons {btns}  reviews {nrev}")
    return slug

# ── routes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug])
# or when tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json fans it out to many fixed routes
# (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...).
# Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p).
def routes_for(slug):
    f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json"
    if os.path.exists(f):
        return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))]
    return [(ROUTES[slug], {})]

def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader):
    """One route file. Every route passes its [params], fixed template params
    and ?query (search, pagination, ?topic= deep links…) into the loader as one
    map; the concrete path (/mods/[family]/[slug] -> /mods/minecraft/lithium)
    is used for canonical and breadcrumbs."""
    rd = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm{route}"; os.makedirs(rd, exist_ok=True)
    rel = os.path.relpath(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm", rd)
    pc = PARTICLES.get(slug)
    particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else ""
    # loader-supplied colours (e.g. per game) win over the slug default
    pdefault = f' ?? {{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}' if pc else ""
    has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read()
    dyn = "[" in route
    assert not (dyn or fixed) or has_meta, f"{slug}: template routes need a loader with meta(p) for SEO"
    path_expr = ("`" + re.sub(r"\[(\w+)\]", r"${p.\1}", route) + "`") if dyn else json.dumps(route)
    if loader:
        imp = (f'import {{ load{", meta" if has_meta else ""} }} from "{rel}/_data/{slug}";\n'
               f'import type {{ NxmLoad }} from "{rel}/_data/lib";\n'
               f'import {{ nxmParams }} from "{rel}/_data/params";\n')
        ptype = "{ params: Promise<Record<string, string>>; searchParams: Promise<Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>> }"
        getp = f"const p = await nxmParams(params, searchParams, {json.dumps(fixed)});"
        metacall = f"nxmMetadata({path_expr}, await meta(p))" if has_meta else f"nxmMetadata({path_expr})"
        body = f"""export async function generateMetadata({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}): Promise<Metadata> {{
  {getp}
  return {metacall};
}}

export default async function Page({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}) {{
  {getp}
  const d: NxmLoad = await load(p);
  return <NxmPage slug="{slug}" route={{{path_expr}}} body={{C.BODY_HTML}} attrs={{C.BODY_ATTRS}} particles={{d.particles{pdefault}}} slots={{d.slots}} data={{d.data}} jsonLd={{d.jsonLd}} crumb={{d.crumb}} trail={{d.trail}} />;

    else:

}}

export default async function Page() {{

import type {{ Metadata }} from "next";
import {{ NxmPage }} from "{rel}/_components/NxmPage";
import {{ nxmMetadata }} from "{rel}/_seo/meta";
import * as C from "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/content";
{imp}import "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/page.css";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

    slugs = sys.argv[1:] or [s for s in ROUTES if s != "home"]

        + "};\n")

Either path involves duplication, so I lean toward Option A since it requires zero changes to the skin's existing files, just a small README edit in the tools scope to document the split between the frozen skin template and the new general-purpose one.

Other tools' related-tools blocks probably link to the skin creator, which should still work fine. content.content:
| Outcome | Exactly what marks it |
|---|---|
| **renewed** | AuditLog `billing.renewed` (server: detail = server id, written inside `commitRenewal`, which the sweep, admin "Renew now" and the unpaid auto-recovery all use; hosting/email/volume: detail `"<kind> <id> <name> $X -> date"`), or `server.renew_now` (customer button). Joined to its PAID invoice (`Renewal:…`, `Web Hosting renewal:…`, `Business Email renewal:…`, `Block storage renewal:…`) within 20 s for the amount and `periodStart` (= due date). Domains: WalletTransaction `Domain renewal: <name> …` debits. *Recovered* = paid after a failed attempt in the same period; *early* = paid > 1 day before due (all admin Renew-now renewals so far). Source = admin when an `admin.renew_now … renewed via …` row follows within 15 s. |
| **failed** (involuntary churn) | Auto-renew was ON at the due date and the money never arrived: `billing.suspended_unpaid` / `billing.terminated_unpaid`, or a removed service whose last period had a failed charge (`billing.card_declined`, `billing.card_unusable_grace`, `admin.renew_now … FAILED — insufficientFunds`), or a live one still unpaid > 14 days after due. Rail = card if any card failure, else wallet. |
| **voluntary** churn | Auto-renew OFF at the due date (state reconstructed from `server.autorenew_toggle` / `server.cancel_period_end` history, else the row's flag), or the customer removed it: `server.delete`, `server.cancel_immediate`, `hosting.cancel`, a cancelled email sub; or the service vanished with no failed charge (incl. no removal record at all). |
| **admin** (removed by Nxeon) | `admin.fraud_teardown`, `billing.reaped_suspended` (ABUSE/ADMIN suspension), `server.cancel_immediate` with an "admin cleanup/teardown" note, `qa.sweep_teardown`. Excluded from every rate. |
| **pending** | Due date passed, nothing collected, not suspended, ≤ 14 days (dunning / card-readd grace). |
| **upcoming** | Due date in the future (the current `expiresAt`). |

**When a cycle counts:** at `decidedAt` = the earlier of its due date and the moment it was settled (paid / suspended / cancelled). Paid-early renewals count the day they were paid; a cancellation before term end counts the day of the cancellation. Buckets are UTC weeks (Monday start) or calendar months.

**Metrics.** Renewal rate = renewed ÷ (renewed + failed + voluntary). Payment success = renewed ÷ (renewed + failed); failure rate = failed ÷ (renewed + failed). Revenue retained = collected ÷ (collected + expected amount of failed + voluntary cycles). Card attempt decline rate = (declines + unusable-card events) ÷ (those + renewals with a card leg) — attempt-level, so one dunning sequence counts several times. Method of a renewal: the card leg is the `WalletTransaction` credit with a Stripe PaymentIntent described `Card payment for <host> renewal …` within 30 min before the commit (the card funds the wallet, the wallet pays — `attemptCardRenewal`); the admin Renew-now detail's wallet/card split wins when present. PayPal renewals show only if the (off-by-default) `renewals_paypal_fallback_enabled` fallback ever wrote a `PayPal payment for <host> renewal` credit — none exist as of 2026-10-07. Cohort curves: services by start month; renewal *k* = survived ÷ reached, where a service that churned at *j < k* counts as not-survived once its *k*-th due date would have passed; pending / upcoming / admin-removed are censored.

**Amounts.** Upcoming and live-service amounts are what the sweep will charge: VPS/game via `renewalCharge()` (lib/renewal-charge.ts) with the owner's VAT/GST (`resolveCountryTaxRate`) and Creator-Partner rate (`partnerDiscountForRenewal`) — i.e. tax-INCLUSIVE and discount-NET, add-ons (dedicated IP, extra disk, backup tier) included; hosting `hostingRenewalPrice()` − partner discount; email `productTermRenewalCents(emailMonthlyBaseCents…)` − partner (same primitives as the private `emailRenewalPrice` in the worker); domains `domainTermPriceCents(renewPriceCents ?? priceCents)`; volumes `volumeRenewalCents`. Hosting/email/domain/volume renewals carry no tax (their sweeps add none). Removed services are priced at their last actually-charged renewal, else the order invoice's `renewalCents` snapshot, else the catalog price from the order audit (`plan=` / `tier=`) — marked "est.". "At risk" = auto-renew on, wallet below the amount and no chargeable card (email/domain/volume sweeps are wallet-only, so a card does not help them).

**Removed services are reconstructed** (their `Server` row is deleted and `Job.serverId` is nulled): the `server.order` / `gameserver.order` audit (detail starts with the server id; `term=Nmo`) + the order invoice created within 30 s (hostname from "(host)", `periodEnd` = first due date) + the end events above (by id, or by hostname for `admin.server.delete` / `admin.fraud_teardown`). Removed hosting accounts likewise from `hosting.order` (`"<Plan> · <domain>"`) with the next unmatched `hosting.cancel` of that user.

**Known limits of the data (as of 2026-10-07).**
- Renewal evidence for real customers starts 2026-09-13 (earlier renewals were all on excluded internal accounts); the business is ~10 weeks old, so every rate sits on single-digit counts. `invoice.serverId` only exists since 2026-10-06, so server renewals are joined to invoices by owner + time + hostname.
- `adminTerminateHostingAccount` writes no audit row, so an admin-terminated hosting account looks like "removed, no record" (counted voluntary). Two prod accounts (testing@mail.com, villaverse0) are in that state.
- `admin.server.delete` doesn't say whether the customer or Nxeon asked; it is classified by the failure signals of that period (failed charge → involuntary, else voluntary).
- Email subscriptions have no auto-renew toggle audit; their current flag is used. Hosting always auto-renews.
- Account deletions (GDPR) take their audit rows' `userId` with them, so those services are invisible here.
- Payment `ActivityEvent` rows (`payment.renewal` / `payment.dunning`) exist only since 2026-10-06 and are not used; the AuditLog trail is the longer source.

## Free tools overhaul on the new marketing site: `tools-app` template, shared tool atoms (2026-10-07)

**What changed.** The `/tools` hub and every `/tools/<slug>` page except the Minecraft skin creator were overhauled. URLs, titles, meta descriptions, canonicals and JSON-LD did not change; a before/after curl of all 20 routes matched field for field.

- **Tool pages now use a new template, `tools-app`.** It has a left-aligned editorial hero with an "At a glance" glass card: where the tool runs, the price, and the key that runs it. On phones that card shrinks to one compact block, so the input sits much higher on the page.
  - The tool panel has a footer with an honest privacy line ("Checked live from Nxeon's servers…" or "Runs entirely in your browser…") and the run key.
  - Each page has 4 related-tool cards with mode chips. The live page's own picks come first, topped up from the same category.
  - Each tool has its own icon.
- **The skin creator keeps the original `tools-tool` template, byte for byte.** `tools/nxm/routes/tools-tool.json` now lists only `/tools/minecraft-skin-creator`. Its generated `app/nxm/_pages/tools-tool/*`, its route file and its loader `app/nxm/_data/tools-tool.ts` were not changed. Don't merge it into `tools-app` without the owner's say-so.
- **Hub changes:**
  - The result count is announced to screen readers.
  - `?q=` and `?cat=` stay in the URL, so a filtered view can be shared.
  - `/` focuses search, and Enter opens the first match.
  - "No match" shows clickable suggestions.
  - Each tool has its own icon.
  - The heading "Servers tools" now reads "Server tools".
- **Shared tool components** (`components/marketing/tools/*`, also used by the rollback `app/(marketing)/tools` pages, so they keep their Tailwind classes):
  - One-click example inputs (`Examples`) on DNS, WHOIS, port, SSL, HTTP headers, Minecraft status, subnet, hash and domain-generator briefs. Network examples run immediately.
  - Empty, loading and error states (`EmptyState`, `LoadingRows`, `ErrorNote role=alert`). Results sit in `aria-live` regions.
  - A copy button on every copyable result: per-row copy in `KeyValue` (3rd tuple item), "Copy all records", "Copy headers", "Copy report", "Copy summary" and so on. The plain-text formats live in `lib/tools/result-text.ts`.
  - Enter submits every form. `Ctrl/Cmd+Enter` formats JSON (with Shift it minifies) and runs the domain generator.
  - Per-tool extras:
    - Port checker: pasting `host:port` fills both fields.
    - JSON errors: show line and column.
    - JSON formatter: the "Tab" indent now uses a real tab.
    - Base64: sample, swap and clear buttons, plus byte counts.
    - Password generator: length presets and a mobile-safe output.
    - UUID generator: count presets.
    - Latency test: a Stop button, per-sample bars, and copyable results.
    - Palworld and Valheim generators: "Reset to defaults", a count of changed options, and `.ini`/`.env` downloads.
    - My IP: Refresh/Try again, plus a copyable curl command.
    - Size calculator: "Copy link to this sizing" (`?workload=&players=`).
- **Styling.** The `tl-*` hook classes on the atoms are restyled only by CSS scoped to `.tt-app` in `tools/nxm/native/tools-app/page.css`, using the Aurora tokens: cyan for live/active, green/red/amber only for semantic state.

**Where things live.**
- **Hub:** `tools/nxm/native/tools/*` (generator input) and `app/nxm/_data/tools.ts` (loader).
- **Tool template:**
  - Generator input: `tools/nxm/native/tools-app/{body.html,page.css,page.js,meta.json}`, `tools/nxm/wire/tools_app.py` and `tools/nxm/routes/tools-app.json`.
  - Loader: `app/nxm/_data/tools-app.ts`, which also feeds the size calculator's plan data.
  - Presentation data: `app/nxm/_data/tools-ui.ts`, which holds the icon per tool, the run-key hints, the privacy line, the related-tool picker and the hub heading fix.
- **Copy and SEO:** still read from the live pages by `app/nxm/_data/tools-live.ts`. Nothing is hardcoded.
- **Regenerate:** `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py tools tools-app`. Never hand-edit `app/nxm/_pages/tools*/` or `app/nxm/tools/*/page.tsx`.
- **Test:** `test/nxm-tools.test.ts` checks that every catalogue tool is routed exactly once with the right template, has an icon, a privacy line and 4 related tools, and that the copy helpers produce exact text.

**Adding a tool.**
1. Add it to `lib/tools/catalog.ts`.
2. Build the component in `components/marketing/tools/`, using the `ui.tsx` atoms (`Field`, `RunButton` in a `<form>` so Enter works, `Examples`, `EmptyState`, `CopyButton`).
3. Add the live page `app/(marketing)/tools/<slug>/page.tsx` using `ToolShell` for copy, FAQ and SEO, and register it in `LIVE` in `tools-live.ts`.
4. Register the component in `app/nxm/_components/ToolMount.tsx`.
5. Add an icon and, if it has one, a run key in `tools-ui.ts`.
6. Add the route to `tools/nxm/routes/tools-app.json`.
7. Run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py tools tools-app`, then `npx tsx scripts/nxm-live-routes.ts`.
8. Run `tsx --test test/nxm-tools.test.ts`.

## Tools overhaul: done, committed as `852d6fcf62` on fix/portal-batch-2026-10-07 (61 files, explicit paths only)

The `/tools` hub and all 18 tool pages are overhauled. The Minecraft skin creator is untouched, and SEO did not change on any route. Tests and `tsc --noEmit -p .` are clean. Nothing was pushed, merged or deployed.

**How the skin creator was protected.** The skin creator and the other tools shared one page template, so changing that template would have changed the skin page too. I split them:
- The old template, `tools-tool`, now serves only `/tools/minecraft-skin-creator`. Its generator input, generated files (`app/nxm/_pages/tools-tool/*`), route file and loader (`_data/tools-tool.ts`) are unchanged.
- A new template, `tools-app`, serves the other 18 tools.
- I checked: the skin page's `<main>` markup is byte-identical before and after.

**Files**
- **New template (generator inputs):** `tools/nxm/native/tools-app/{body.html,page.css,page.js,meta.json}`, `tools/nxm/wire/tools_app.py`, `tools/nxm/routes/tools-app.json` (the 18 routes).
- **Small edits:** `tools-tool.json` now lists only the skin creator; `nxmlib.py` has a 3-line `ROUTES` entry; `tools/nxm/README.md` has a note.
- **New loaders/helpers:**
  - `app/nxm/_data/tools-app.ts`: page loader; also feeds the size calculator's plan data.
  - `app/nxm/_data/tools-ui.ts`: pure, tested helpers — per-tool icons, run-key hints, privacy line, related-tool picker, hub heading fix.
- **Hub:** `tools/nxm/native/tools/*` and `app/nxm/_data/tools.ts`.
- **Shared components:** `components/marketing/tools/ui.tsx` plus all 16 tool components, `lib/tools/result-text.ts` (new: the copy-text formats), `app/nxm/_components/ToolSizeCalculator.tsx`.
- **Regenerated output:** `app/nxm/_pages/tools`, `app/nxm/_pages/tools-app` and 18 route `page.tsx` files, via `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py tools tools-app`. Real-data audit says "wired" for both.
- **Docs:** new section appended to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: "Free tools overhaul on the new marketing site…". It covers where things live and the 8 steps to add a tool.

**UX changes**
- **Every tool page:**
  - Left-aligned hero with an "At a glance" card (where it runs, price, key that runs it). It compacts on phones, so the input is on the first screen at 390px.
  - A panel footer with an honest privacy line ("Checked live from Nxeon's servers" or "Runs entirely in your browser").
  - 4 related-tool cards: the live page's own picks first, then the same category.
  - Its own icon per tool.
- **Hub:**
  - Shows "Showing N of 19 tools", announced to screen readers.
  - `?q=` and `?cat=` stay in the URL; Enter opens the first match.
  - "No match" shows clickable suggestions.
  - "Servers tools" now reads "Server tools".
- **All tools:** labelled inputs, Enter submits, results announced to screen readers, empty/loading/error states, and copy buttons on every copyable result (per row, per card, or copy-all).
- **One-click examples:**
  - DNS, WHOIS, SSL (includes expired.badssl.com), HTTP headers, port (host:port), Minecraft status: these run immediately.
  - Subnet, hash and domain-generator briefs: these fill the input.
- **Per-tool extras:**
  - Port checker: pasting `host:port` fills both fields.
  - JSON formatter: sample, Clear, Ctrl+Enter, line:column on errors, size stats.
  - Base64: sample, Swap, Clear, byte counts.
  - Password generator: length presets and an output that doesn't overflow on phones.
  - UUID generator: count presets.
  - Hash generator: Copy all, uppercase option.
  - Latency test: Stop button, per-sample bars, copyable results.
  - Palworld/Valheim generators: Reset to defaults, a count of changed options, `.ini`/`.env` downloads.
  - My IP: Refresh/Try again, copyable curl command.
  - Minecraft status: §-colour codes stripped from the MOTD.
  - Size calculator: "Copy link to this sizing".
- **One behaviour change to know about:** the JSON "Tab" indent option now inserts a real tab. It used to insert 8 spaces under the label "Tab (8)".

**SEO check.** I curled all 20 routes before any change and again after. Every field matched on every route: status, `<title>`, meta description, canonical, robots, og:title, JSON-LD @types, a hash of the full JSON-LD, and h1. Scripts and data are in `/tmp/claude-0/tools-seo/` (`seo-before.json` vs `seo-final.json`).

**Tests and type check**
- `tsx --test test/nxm-tools.test.ts`: 8/8 pass. It covers: every tool routed exactly once with the right template and unchanged URL, live-routes and metadata present, the hub's registry entry, icons and privacy lines, related-tool rules, the heading fix, and exact copy-text output.
- `test/seo-audit.test.ts` 16/16 and `test/ai-agents-page.test.ts` 10/10 pass.
- `test/api-http-surface.test.ts` has 1 failure that isn't from this work: discord and mod-builder routes throttle on an "unvetted key".
- `tsc --noEmit -p .` was clean, run under the lock.

**Browser checks.** All 19 tool routes plus the hub at 390 and 1440 have no horizontal scroll, and every tool component mounted. One exception: the dns-lookup sweep hit a dev-server connection reset and then reported not-mounted. The DNS interaction screenshots show it mounting and returning results fine.

**Screenshots** (`/root/agent-notes/portal-batch-1007/tools/`):
- `final/`: hub plus 8 tools at 1440 and 390, including the skin creator.
- `state-*`: interaction states.
- `before/`, `r1/`: baselines.
- `rollback/`: the old site (`NXM_ROOT=0`).
- `*-390.png`: every route at 390.
- There is no light-theme capture: the marketing site is dark-only.

The best 4:
1. `state-dns-lookup-1440.png`: live DNS results with per-type and copy-all buttons.
2. `final/server-size-calculator-1440.png`.
3. `state-ssl-checker-390.png`.
4. `final/hub-1440.png`.

**Rollback site check.** The old `app/(marketing)/tools` pages still render correctly with the new components. At 390 those pages scroll 4px sideways (394px). The overflowing element isn't inside the tool content; the rollback header looks crowded at that width, but I didn't confirm the culprit or check whether it predates my change. I left it alone (outside scope).

**Data and cleanup**
- I copied the Plan (25) and GamePlan (142) rows from prod into the throwaway `nxeon_pb1007` DB. The prod side ran inside a `READ ONLY` transaction; the throwaway side used inserts only.
- I didn't touch /opt/nxeon, the skin creator's files or its markup. Every dev server was killed by its own PID.

**Decisions for you or the owner**
1. Should the skin creator eventually move to `tools-app` too? I left it on the old template because you said not to touch it.
2. The JSON tab change above.
3. The example inputs use public third-party hosts (github.com, gmail.com, wikipedia.org, mc.hypixel.net, play.cubecraft.net, expired.badssl.com) next to nxeon.cloud. Swap them if the owner prefers.

**Possible cleanup.** The old loader `app/nxm/_data/tools-tool.ts` still contains the size-calculator code, which is now unused there. I left it untouched to keep the skin creator's files identical.
